customer_question: Do we need separate compliance folder documents (manual, block diagram, outline drawing) for every model, or can they be shared? And how detailed does the block diagram actually need to be?
question_variants: If we register multiple models at once, do we need documents for each?
Can we use one generic block diagram for similar devices instead of a model-specific one?
How much detail is expected in the block diagram?
actual_issue: The customer needed to know whether compliance folder documents were required per individual model or could be shared across models, and how much technical detail the product block diagram specifically needed to contain, since it was unclear whether a generic diagram for similar-purpose devices would be acceptable.
plain_english_explanation: Whether you need separate paperwork for each product model depends on how many models you actually listed when you first registered. If you only listed one representative model up front, you only need documents for that one model. If you listed several models at once, you'll need documents covering each of them. And for the block diagram specifically, it doesn't need to be a precise, detailed engineering schematic -- a general-purpose diagram showing roughly how the device works is good enough, similar to what you'd see published online for a comparable product.
consultant_answer: If only one representative model is listed in the initial registration's Product List, the compliance folder only needs that one model's documents. If multiple models are listed in the initial registration, documents are needed for each of those models. As for the block diagram's level of detail, a sample block diagram for a publicly-available USB Bluetooth Audio Receiver product was provided as a reference, illustrating that a general, representative-level diagram is sufficient rather than a precise, model-specific engineering schematic.
decision_logic: Compliance folder documentation scope is determined by how many models are listed in the initial registration's Product List -- one representative model requires only that model's documents, while multiple models listed at initial registration each require their own documents. Block diagrams are accepted at a generic, representative level of detail, illustrated by reference to a comparable publicly-available product's diagram, rather than requiring a precise, model-specific engineering schematic.
final_recommendation: Clarify with the customer how many models will be listed in the initial registration to determine compliance folder document scope, and provide a reference example (such as a comparable public product's block diagram) to set expectations that a generic, representative-level diagram is acceptable rather than a detailed engineering schematic.
risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming one set of documents covers every model in a multi-model initial registration, or insisting on an overly detailed block diagram, could result in either an incomplete compliance folder or unnecessary extra documentation work.
